# gns3_node (Resource)

A node in a GNS3 project, created from a template (`template_id`) or directly from an emulator type (`node_type` with `compute_id` and `properties`). Exactly one of `template_id` and `node_type` must be set. The node's ports are read back after create so `gns3_link` can reference them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "gns3_project" "lab" {
  name = "tf-example-node"
}

# Built-in VPCS template: no image to download.
data "gns3_template" "vpcs" {
  name = "VPCS"
}

# startup_config is written to the node's startup.vpc and read back on
# refresh. Editing startup.vpc beside this file updates the node in place; the
# new config takes effect the next time the node starts.
resource "gns3_node" "pc1" {
  project_id     = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  template_id    = data.gns3_template.vpcs.template_id
  name           = "PC1"
  x              = -150
  y              = 0
  startup_config = file("${path.module}/startup.vpc")
}

# A template-less node: node_type, compute_id and emulator properties.
resource "gns3_node" "pc2" {
  project_id = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  node_type  = "vpcs"
  compute_id = "local"
  name       = "PC2"
  x          = 150
  y          = 0
  properties = jsonencode({ startup_script = "set pcname PC2" })
}

output "pc1_console" {
  value = gns3_node.pc1.console
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Node name, unique within the project.
- `project_id` (String) Project UUID. Changing it replaces the node.

### Optional

- `compute_id` (String) Compute to run the node on. When unset, `local` is sent; a template with its own compute keeps it. Changing it replaces the node.
- `console_type` (String) Console type: one of `vnc`, `telnet`, `http`, `https`, `spice`, `spice+agent`, `none`. The template or node type default when unset.
- `node_type` (String) Emulator type for a template-less node: one of `cloud`, `nat`, `ethernet_hub`, `ethernet_switch`, `frame_relay_switch`, `atm_switch`, `docker`, `dynamips`, `vpcs`, `traceng`, `virtualbox`, `vmware`, `iou`, `qemu`. Read from the server when `template_id` is used. Changing it replaces the node.
- `properties` (String) Emulator-specific properties as a JSON object (use `jsonencode`), only with `node_type`. Only the keys you set are compared with the server, so server-side defaults do not show as drift. For `vpcs`, `startup_script` is written to and read from the node's `startup.vpc` file rather than sent as a property, because GNS3 2.2 rejects it in node updates. It cannot be combined with `startup_config`. For `dynamips`, `startup_config_content` and `private_config_content` are refused: GNS3 2.2 accepts them at create but then fails every later update of the node; use `startup_config` instead.
- `start_on_create` (Boolean) Start the node right after it is created. Only acts at create; later changes are recorded but do not start or stop the node. Default `false`.
- `startup_config` (String) Day-zero configuration as text; keep it in a file with `file("${path.module}/startup.vpc")`. The provider picks where it goes from the node type and writes it through the node files endpoint: `vpcs` → `startup.vpc`, `dynamips` → `configs/i<dynamips_id>_startup-config.cfg` in the node directory. It is read back on refresh, so changes made on the server show as drift. On create it is written before the node is started (`start_on_create`). A change is applied in place and takes effect the next time the node starts; a running node is not restarted. Removing the attribute stops managing the file and leaves its content. `qemu` is not supported (GNS3 2.2 config disks do not work on Windows computes and are not read by VyOS; configure the appliance after boot with Ansible, or with cloud-init where the image supports it), and `iou` and `docker` are not supported yet: setting it on those, or on any other node type, is an error, at plan time when the node type (or the template's type) is known.
- `symbol` (String) Symbol path, for example `:/symbols/computer.svg`. The template or node type default when unset.
- `template_id` (String) Template UUID to create the node from: `template_id` of a `gns3_template` resource (a template the configuration manages) or data source (a built-in or existing one). Changing it replaces the node.
- `x` (Number) X position on the drawing area. Default `0`.
- `y` (Number) Y position on the drawing area. Default `0`.
- `z` (Number) Z order on the drawing area. Default `1`.

### Read-Only

- `console` (Number) Console TCP port, null when the node has no console.
- `node_id` (String) Node UUID assigned by the server.
- `ports` (Attributes List) The node's ports as reported by the server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ports))
- `status` (String) `stopped`, `started` or `suspended`, as last read from the server.

<a id="nestedatt--ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ports`

Read-Only:

- `adapter_number` (Number) Adapter number.
- `link_type` (String) `ethernet` or `serial`.
- `name` (String) Port name, for example `Ethernet0`.
- `port_number` (Number) Port number on the adapter.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <project_id>/<node_id>.
terraform import gns3_node.pc1 2d37e1d1-0bbd-4525-8777-529b1bba7f85/3e1037e1-343f-44ea-8b7f-a653eb2d94cf
```
